events.title: 40th Anniversary of Franklin in the Dark
events.description: First published in 1986, join us in celebrating 40 years of the beloved Canadian turtle, Franklin. Discover the series’ original drafts by author Paulette Bourgeois and illustrator Brenda Clark, alongside other terrific turtle tales! Visit the Osborne Collection to experience our exhibit.

events.title: Celebrate 60 years of Mimico Centennial Library
events.description: Throughout November, we're celebrating the 60th anniversary of Mimico Centennial Library ! Take a walk through history with our special historical photo display , featuring images and newspaper articles of the library and surrounding Mimico community through the years. Discover how our neighbourhood has changed and revisit the people, places, and moments that have shaped our community.  60 years of stories. 60 years of memories. 60 years of community.

events.title: Nocturnal Animals Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Welcome to the Night Shift! Stop by the library to find images of nocturnal animals hidden around the children's area. Find them all and win a fun prize! This program is intended for children aged 4 to 12 years .

events.title: Game on! Board Game Playtime
events.description: Join us for a fun-filled day of board games and puzzles! Play your favourites or try something new! Brings your friends and family or meet new people at the library. Games available for use in the Children's Area. Available games include: Ball Fall Jumbo (Ages 3+), STEM Pretend Flower Garden Toy Set (Ages 3-6), Operation (Ages 6+), STEM Road Builder Game (Ages 4-8), Dinosaur Tetra Tower Balance Stacking Blocks Game (Ages 6+) Available puzzles include: Giant World Map Puzzle (

events.title: Crafturday
events.description: Join us for a day of fun and crafts. Partake in a new and engaging craft every Saturday from 9:30am - 4:30pm. Drop-in and self-serve. For pre-school and school-aged children and their caregivers.

events.title: Builders Club
events.description: Do you like to build with LEGO, DUPLO, Feltro, Snap Circuits or KEVA? Join us every Saturday morning for some fun building challenges! All children welcome with their caregivers. Drop-in, no registration required.

events.title: Book Launch: Stories We Couldn’t Keep to Ourselves, presented by Story Planet
events.description: Story Planet is proud to present, “Stories we couldn’t keep to ourselves”. A magical collection of picture books written and illustrated by Young KGO Authors. You’re invited to a very special book launch! Join us in celebrating these talented young authors with story readings and activities for the whole family!  All ages welcome! Registration required

events.title: Saturday Morning Movies
events.description: Come join us for a Saturday morning movie. Bring your own snacks and enjoy our feature film.  Drop-in. No registration required. For ages 0-12 accompanied by a parent or caregiver. Oct. 31 - The Book of Life (2014) Nov. 7: Cars (2006) Nov. 14: Planes (2013) Nov. 21: Bad Guys (2022) Nov. 28: Bad Guys 2 (2025)

events.title: Builder's Club
events.description: Join us on Saturday mornings and build to your heart’s content!  LEGO, DUPLO, and KEVA planks will be provided for you to explore your creativity. All children welcome with their caregivers. Drop-in, no registration required.

events.title: Building buddies
events.description: Are you a curious and creative buddy who likes to build and create something new using all kind of materials?  Than, come to our program where you can build unique and amazing structures using different materials like LEGO, KEVA blocks, and/or other materials. All materials will be provided.  For children ages 5-12.  Drop-in program, no registration required.

events.title: 3D Printing Demo Drop-in
events.description: Watch one of Toronto Public Library's 3D printer in action, see samples, learn how they work, and how you can use them at TPL Digital Innovation Hubs. Drop-in at anytime during the demo!

events.title: Maker's Club
events.description: Join us for self-directed STEM activity each week!

events.title: Family Movies - The Land of Sometimes
events.description: Every other Saturday Cliffcrest will be screening a free family friendly movie! This months' movie: The Land of Sometimes The Land Of Sometimes is an animated musical adventure following twins, Alfie and Elise, as they are whisked away by The Wish Collector to have all their wishes come true. Join them on a journey through a magical land as they meet fantastical characters and charming creatures that guide them to become their better selves.

events.title: Family Time

Come out to build, create and code with Snap Circuits, Dash and Dot, Scratch Coding, LEGO, Magnetic Tiles and more! The club is intended for children aged 6 to 12 years. Due to the limited number of robots, participants may be asked to share with other participants. Drop-in. No registration is required.

events.title: Saturday Chess Club
events.description: Join us on the 2nd floor every Saturday for a few games of chess in a welcoming environment. All ages and all levels are welcome. Children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian to participate. Any unsupervised individuals under 18 will not be able to participate in the program. Please note: There is no chess club on Sat Nov 21 for our Big Fall Book Sale This is a drop-in program.

events.title: LEGO CLUB
events.description: Are you a fan of LEGO? Join your friends to explore, create and build from your imagination or one of our challenges. Younger children may come and play with our Duplo or Mega Blocks. Drop-in!

events.title: STEAM Lab
events.description: Join us for our weekly STEAM Lab (Ages 6-12) , where kids can explore science, technology, engineering, art, and math through fun, hands-on activities. From building simple robots and experimenting with Snap Circuits to creative design challenges and more, there’s always something new to discover. Activities change each week, so there’s always something new to explore!

events.title: STEM Sundays
events.description: Explore a different STEM-themed activity every Sunday the library is open. Topics include robotics, circuitry, building and more! For children aged 6-12 and their caregivers. Drop in.

events.title: Sunday Lego Club
events.description: Join us each Sunday (barring scheduled closures) to build LEGO structures and have fun at the Forest Hill library! For children under 12 years and their families. Please ensure young children are accompanied by an adult.

events.title: After School Club
events.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids, and have fun!  Drop-in. For ages 6-12. events.title: STEM Club
events.description: Join us at the library for a fun hour of stem related activities. Come out to build, create and code with Snap Circuits, Dash and Dot, Scratch Coding, LEGO, Magnetic Tiles and more! The club is intended for children aged 6 to 12 years. Due to the limited number of robots, participants may be asked to share with other participants. Drop-in. No registration is required.

events.title: LEGO CLUB
events.description: Are you a fan of LEGO? Join your friends to explore, create and build from your imagination or one of our challenges. Younger children may come and play with our Duplo or Mega Blocks. Drop-in!

events.title: STEAM Lab
events.description: Join us for our weekly STEAM Lab (Ages 6-12) , where kids can explore science, technology, engineering, art, and math through fun, hands-on activities. From building simple robots and experimenting with Snap Circuits to creative design challenges and more, there’s always something new to discover. Activities change each week, so there’s always something new to explore!

events.title: STEM Sundays
events.description: Explore a different STEM-themed activity every Sunday the library is open. Topics include robotics, circuitry, building and more! For children aged 6-12 and their caregivers. Drop in.

events.title: Sunday Lego Club
events.description: Join us each Sunday (barring scheduled closures) to build LEGO structures and have fun at the Forest Hill library! For children under 12 years and their families. Please ensure young children are accompanied by an adult.

events.title: March Break with Swallowing Clouds
events.description: Join us for this program where together, we will use improv, music, storytelling, arts & crafts, and movement to create our own work of creative-movement theatre. Children will work with professional dancers, musicians and authors, and will be guided through an inspiring creative journey. In this program, we focus on: Building confidence Developing friends Including everyone Sharing ideas Expanding creativity Limited space available. Register online. For children ages 9-12. events.title: 40th Anniversary of Franklin in the Dark
events.description: First published in 1986, join us in celebrating 40 years of the beloved Canadian turtle, Franklin. Discover the series’ original drafts by author Paulette Bourgeois and illustrator Brenda Clark, alongside other terrific turtle tales! Visit the Osborne Collection to experience our exhibit.

events.title: Celebrate 60 years of Mimico Centennial Library
events.description: Throughout November, we're celebrating the 60th anniversary of Mimico Centennial Library ! Take a walk through history with our special historical photo display , featuring images and newspaper articles of the library and surrounding Mimico community through the years. Discover how our neighbourhood has changed and revisit the people, places, and moments that have shaped our community.  60 years of stories. 60 years of memories. 60 years of community.

events.title: Video Editing with Da Vinci Resolve Parts I and II
events.description: This two part introductory series will cover the layout, tools and workflow used for video editing in DaVinci Resolve. Part I, which will take place on November 10th , will cover basic video editing techniques such as inserting and trimming media, transitions, titles, adding audio, and using flags and markers. Part II will be held on November 17th , where participants will become familiar with some of the more advanced tools in DaVinci’s Editing page such as key framing

events.title: Knitting Circle
events.description: Join Port Union Library's Knitting Circle. Chat and knit or crochet with a friendly group! You can also share your projects with others!  This is a drop in program but limited to a room capacity of 20 participants. Arrive early to secure your spot.  No registration required.

events.title: Introduction to Machine Embroidery
events.description: Learn how to use the Brother Persona PRS100 at the Fabrication Studio! This class will walk you through the basics of mounting fabric onto the embroidery frames and threading the machine. This course is mandatory in order to book the embroidery machine and will be held in the Fabrication Studio on the 2nd floor. Children under 13 must be accompanied by an adult. Registration is required for this class and begins October 31, 2026 at 12:30 pm. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes

events.title: Book Launch: Stories We Couldn’t Keep to Ourselves, presented by Story Planet
events.description: Story Planet is proud to present, “Stories we couldn’t keep to ourselves”. A magical collection of picture books written and illustrated by Young KGO Authors. You’re invited to a very special book launch! Join us in celebrating these talented young authors with story readings and activities for the whole family!  All ages welcome! Registration required

events.title: 3D Printing Demo Drop-in
events.description: Watch one of Toronto Public Library's 3D printer in action, see samples, learn how they work, and how you can use them at TPL Digital Innovation Hubs. Drop-in at anytime during the demo!

events.title: FRESH Movie Saturdays
events.description: This program helps people stay active, make friends, learn new skills, and have fun. Meet new folks, build connections, and tell us about programs and services you would like to see in the neighbourhood! Come join us every Saturday for screenings of your favourite movies. In addition to this, enjoy cuddles with a therapy dog! Therapy dog Goose visits Fort York Branch on alternate Saturdays from 11:00AM-12:00PM. We'll be showing the following films: Nov 14 - Africa-An Cats Nov 21 - The

events.title: Saturday Chess Club
events.description: Join us on the 2nd floor every Saturday for a few games of chess in a welcoming environment. All ages and all levels are welcome. Children must be accompanied by a parent or guardian to participate. Any unsupervised individuals under 18 will not be able to participate in the program. Please note: There is no chess club on Sat Nov 21 for our Big Fall Book Sale This is a drop-in program.

events.title: Jigsaw Puzzle Social & Swap
events.description: Join other local jigsaw puzzle enthusiasts for an afternoon of communal puzzling. Bring your own puzzle or try out one of the puzzles provided. Drop-in anytime from 2-4PM. Have a puzzle you aren’t using anymore? Bring it in & swap it for another to take home with you. Please note that the puzzle swap will only take place during the program time.

events.title: Artists in the Library:  Fly Agaric Mushroom Felt Collage
events.description: Part 3 of a series of workshops for children and adults, exploring local flora through embroidery and felt collage. This event is part of the  Artists in the Library program, hosted by Artist, Sarah Zanchetta. All ages program; children ages 6 to 14 must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver. Registration is required. Space is limited. Note: Each workshop requires separate registration. Registered participant spaces are held for 15 minutes after which drop-ins are allowed Meet the Re

events.title: Artists in the Library: Community Animation Screening
events.description: Join us for an open community screening of the Brentwood participant artists' short stop-motion animation film. This event is part of the  Artists in the Library Program

events.title: Linocut Printmaking drop-in studio
events.description: Design, carve, ink, and print a linocut print from start to finish in one drop in session led by Ana Gabriela Lopez Castro of AGLCreative Studio . Participants will have the opportunity to display their creations at Main Street Branch in early December. This event is part of the Artists in the Library program.  Free program, no registration is required. Space for each studio session is limited. All participants must be 13 years of age or older. events.title: Knights in the Library
events.description: Knights in the Library is a casual drop-in chess program open to players of all ages and skill levels. Stop by to play a friendly game, practice your strategy, and meet other chess enthusiasts in the community. Whether you are a beginner learning the basics or an experienced player looking for a challenge, everyone is welcome at the board. Families are welcome. Children should be able to play independently and are expected to use respectful library behaviour so everyone can enjoy their games. Ca

events.title: Suddenly They Heard Footsteps: Storytelling with Dan Yashinsky
events.description: Enjoy the art of storytelling as Dan Yashinsky tells folktales, riddles, wisdom stories, and yarns about his trouble-making Romanian-Jewish grandpa. This all-ages program features stories with suspense, surprises, and hilarious suddenlies. Bring your best riddles - there will be a contest! Dan Yashinsky is a storyteller and writer based in Toronto. His books include The Golden Apples , I Am Full – Stories for Jacob , and Suddenly They Heard Footsteps – Storytelling for the Twenty-first Century .

events.title: Spoken Word For Teens: Worldbuilding in Poetry
events.description: Coach & poet Shelly Campbell teaches participants techniques for worldbuilding in poetry. Participants will learn how to imagine and analyze different worlds through the concepts of utopias and dystopias, and explore how poetry can be used to challenge inequality and rewrite history. Drop-in!

events.title: Virtual Reality Demo
events.description: This Drop-In demonstration is for patrons over the age of 13 years old. Leap into the world of virtual reality at the library! Join this drop-in session to try out the Meta Quest virtual reality headset and immerse yourself in stunning 360-degree environments, engage in captivating adventures, and interact with the virtual world.

events.title: Paperback Rebinding for Teens and Young Adults
events.description: Rebind a well loved paperback into a hardcover at the Lillian H Smith library! We will walk you through the process of customizing your beloved book with all materials provided, just bring in your own book! Please note this process is very labour intensive and requires commitment to both sessions (November 14 and 28) and optionally, your own time designing a book cover and/or foredge stencils.  November 14 2-4:30pm - Part 1 Preparing the book, customize the book (en

events.description: Make your very own edible slime workshop! Tap into your five senses, get creative, and learn about mindfulness while crafting a delicious treat that you can take home. All ingredients and equipment will be provided. This workshop is part of the Teen Social Health and Wellness programming. Generously supported by The Estate of Claudia Krawchuk. For ages 13-17. events.title: Love, Lust and Lore: A Merril Collection Exhibit
events.description: Discover tales as old as time. This exhibit celebrates romantasy treasures in the Merril Collection as well as new favourites, role playing games and more! Explore spectacular tales of romance between humans, shapeshifters, monsters and aliens. This exhibit can be viewed during the Merril Collection's regular open hours.

events.description: Join us Sunday to have some fun here at the library.  Try out some Snap Circuits, play a board game, or work on a puzzle. Bring your friends.

events.title: Sunday Family Club
events.description: Enjoy and have fun on Sunday afternoons at Guildwood Library! Will you colour your favourite characters, do a craft or show off your building skills with LEGO and KEVA? Maybe it will be Snap Circuits or Board Games? Every Sunday come in for a surprise!

events.title: Sunday Social Art Hub
events.description: Create your masterpiece using acrylic paint.  Learn how to make zentagles or enjoy colouring.

events.description: Come in and have fun by exploring various building materials and technologies like Dash & Dot, LEGO, Snap Circuits and Sphero BOLT .  All ages, drop in!

events.description: The Chess Institute of Canada is bringing chess to life at your local library!  Join us as we explore the ancient game of chess and the essential life-skills the game imparts. Come and take in a lesson on the great game or sit down and start playing!  Learn, compete, connect with your community through the game of chess. Open to all ages. Children under 12 need to be supervised.

events.description: Join us for creative group activities that support mental wellness, social connection and a sense of belonging. Enjoy music, movement, mindfulness and more while connecting with others and engaging with your community. Drop-in, no registration is required.  TTC Presto tickets will be provided upon request.  Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. events.title: Family Connections: Workshops for Social & Family Support
events.description: Join us for a series of group workshops for anyone navigating relationships, caregiving responsibilities or family dynamics. Explore the impact these experiences can have on mental health and well-being, learn practical strategies, and connect with others in a supportive, non-judgmental environment. Some workshops are co-facilitated by CMHA Toronto’s Family Support Team, bringing together professional expertise and lived experience to support honest, practical and compassionate conversations.&nb
